Audited from `preloader-android-main.zip` (arm64 Bedrock preloader, \~18.6k lines in `src/`).


## Read this first


**What I did.** I read the performance-critical paths in full: signature scanner, hook manager, vtable resolver, player-render hook, local-player feed, frame pacing, snapshot channel, input bridge, all nine Optifine-mode items, startup entry, JNI attach, and the CMake file. That is roughly a fifth of the source (about 3,500 lines). I did **not** fully read `ModMenuBridge.cpp`, `GameCosmetics*.cpp`, `mce_image_hook.cpp`, `AntEggLoader.cpp`, `ExternalModBridgeJni.cpp`, `BerryApi*`, the model parser or the animation solver. Items 194-200 are audits of those. I did not compile or run anything, so every performance claim is a hypothesis to measure, not a result.


**Exact bug count: 33 confirmed bugs.** 32 are in code (items 1-32) and 1 is in CMake (item 107). "Confirmed" means I can point at the line and explain the failure. Some are *latent* (the code is wrong but I cannot show it crashes today); those say so. This is a lower bound, because most of the code is unread.


**About "90% FPS boost".** This library cannot deliver that, and I will not put a number on it. The preloader is not the renderer. In the current code, only three Optifine items touch performance at all (CPU affinity, real-time priority, refresh-rate request). The other four "tier-2" items (entity culling, particle culling, OreUI stripping, callback trimming) are counters that forward the call and cull nothing. Dynamic render distance computes a number and never applies it. The allocator item is disabled. The 4 counting hooks add a little overhead for zero benefit. Real FPS gains come from section D (hooking the swap chain, finding the options setter, culling entities using the already-verified `Actor+0x230` position), and each needs reverse engineering plus measurement (item 149 comes first).


**Tags.** `[BUG]` confirmed defect. `[PERF]` confirmed inefficiency. `[BUILD]` build/link. `[FPS]` roadmap, needs RE and profiling, unverified. `[QUAL]` tests, API, observability, audits.


**Sections.** A: bugs (1-32). B: hot-path and startup cost (33-80). C: build and link (81-110). D: real FPS work (111-160). E: quality and audits (161-200).


## A. Confirmed bugs (1-32)


1. **\[BUG\] GamePlayerRender.cpp:122.** Change `now - last &gt; 1000` to a frame-boundary test (gap of about 3 ms, the same floor used at :136, or a swap hook). `g_renderTick` currently only advances after a 1-second stall, yet AGENTS.md says cape/pet physics runs on it, so that clock is effectively frozen during play.
2. **\[BUG\] SnapshotChannel.hpp:75-76.** Add `std::atomic_thread_fence(std::memory_order_release)` after the odd-sequence store. A release store does not stop the following `memcpy` from being ordered before it on ARM64, so a reader can see a half-written payload with an even sequence.
3. **\[BUG\] SnapshotChannel.hpp:98-107.** Add `std::atomic_thread_fence(std::memory_order_acquire)` before re-reading `sequence_`. The copy sits between two loads that do not order the plain `memcpy`, so the "consistent copy" guarantee does not hold.
4. **\[BUG\] SnapshotChannel.hpp:81.** Replace the plain `memcpy` into `buffer_` with relaxed atomic 64-bit word stores/loads. Concurrent plain read and write is a data race (UB) even when the seqlock discards the result.
5. **\[BUG\] GameLocalPlayer.cpp:84-88.** Add a release fence after the odd `fetch_add`. The acquire half of `acq_rel` does not keep the later plain float stores after the store half.
6. **\[BUG\] GameLocalPlayer.cpp:103-105.** Change `if ((s1 &amp; 1) != 0) return false` to retry a few times. As written, the UI thread reports "no player" whenever it lands inside a write window.
7. **\[BUG\] GameLocalPlayer.cpp:50-51,106-107.** Make `g_position`/`g_rotation` relaxed atomics (or atomic words). They are plain floats read and written concurrently.
8. **\[BUG\] FramePacing.hpp:119-121.** `percentileFirstUs_` is set once (when the count is 0) and never advances, so the span used for `hitchesPerMinute` grows forever while the window holds 2000 samples. Use the timestamp of the oldest sample still in the ring. The doc comment promises a long session will not dilute a burst; the code does the opposite.
9. **\[BUG\] FramePacing.hpp:176.** `percentiles()` is `const` but sorts into the shared `mutable scratch_`. Two concurrent callers corrupt each other. Use a local buffer or a reader mutex.
10. **\[BUG\] FramePacing.hpp:175.** `percentiles()` reads `percentileRing_` while the render thread writes it, a data race. Publish a copy through the (fixed) snapshot channel instead.
11. **\[BUG\] OptifineProcess.cpp:63.** Change the lower-cased substring `find` to an exact match, or better, record the render tid with `gettid()` inside `HookRender`. `"Render"` matches any thread whose name contains "render", including Android's HWUI `RenderThread`, so the real-time boost can land on the wrong thread.
12. **\[BUG\] OptifineRenderPriority.cpp:29.** Delete `"Minecraft Render"`. Thread names in `/proc/.../comm` are capped at 15 characters and this string is 16, so it can never match.
13. **\[BUG\] OptifineRenderPriority.cpp:65.** `gRenderTid` is cached and never revalidated. Check that `/proc/self/task/&lt;tid&gt;` still exists and has the expected name before reporting Active (the render thread can be recreated).
14. **\[BUG\] OptifineRefreshRate.cpp:27,52 / OptifineRenderPriority.cpp:34-35 / OptifineCpuAffinity.cpp:30-31.** Change plain `int`/`bool`/`pid_t` globals to `std::atomic`. `gRequestedHz` is written from the launcher's JNI thread and read by the apply pass; the others are read and written by whichever thread runs the apply pass. These are unsynchronised data races.
15. **\[BUG\] OptifineCpuAffinity.cpp:60.** It pins `gettid()` of whichever thread ran the apply pass and assumes that is the game's main thread. Verify (`gettid() == getpid()`) or pin the render tid recorded by the render hook.
16. **\[BUG\] OptifineProcess.cpp:120.** `freq*10 &gt;= fastest*9` selects only cores within 10% of the fastest. On tri-cluster SoCs where "gold" cores run at roughly 85-90% of the prime core this likely selects 1-2 cores and the item reports "need 4+" and skips. Cluster by the largest frequency gap, or read `/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpuN/cpu_capacity`.
17. **\[BUG\] OptifineProcess.cpp:94.** `break` on the first missing `cpuinfo_max_freq` truncates the core list when an offline core has no cpufreq directory. Use `continue` over `/sys/devices/system/cpu/present`.
18. **\[BUG\] OptifineMode.cpp:157-169.** `ApplyOptifineModeEarly` holds `gStateMutex` while running `/proc` scans and syscalls, so `ReadOptifineState`/`IsOptifineModeActive` block behind them. Do the work outside the lock and publish results under it.
19. **\[BUG\] OptifineRenderDistance.cpp:49 and OptifineMode.cpp:131.** The item reports status Active ("render distance governor: N chunks") although nothing is applied (the file header admits this), and it is added to the applied-items blob the launcher stores. Add a distinct "measuring only" status and keep it out of that blob.
20. **\[BUG\] OptifineEntityCulling.cpp:56, OptifineParticleCulling.cpp:48, OptifineOreUiStripping.cpp:48, OptifineCallbackTrimming.cpp:49.** These four items are named "culling"/"stripping"/"trimming" but only count calls. Rename them to "probe" or implement them, and report a distinct status so a user enabling them is not told a feature is active.
21. **\[BUG, latent\] The four Optifine detours (e.g. OptifineEntityCulling.cpp:42-54).** They are C functions taking 8 `uintptr_t` and returning one. That drops `x8` (struct-return pointer), `v0-v7` (float arguments), stack arguments and any non-`x0` return. `RegisterAwareHook.cpp` already contains a correct naked veneer for three other hooks; reuse it.
22. **\[BUG, latent\] GamePlayerRender.cpp:49,117.** Same ABI loss in `HookRender` (`void(*)(8 pointers)`): a non-void return or float argument of the real function is clobbered.
23. **\[BUG\] Signature.cpp:596.** Disk-cache hits return early, before the in-memory `sigCache` insert at :629-634, so they are never memoised. Every later `resolveSignature` call re-opens and re-parses the `.sigcache` file.
24. **\[BUG\] Signature.cpp:503-509.** A short `process_vm_readv` read (one unreadable page) skips the rest of that 1 MB window. A signature located after the bad page in the same window is missed. Scan the bytes read, then resume after the faulting page.
25. **\[BUG\] Signature.cpp:302.** `std::ofstream(... trunc)` is not atomic; a kill mid-write leaves a truncated cache. Write to a temp file and `rename(2)` over the target.
26. **\[BUG\] Signature.cpp:277-304.** Read-merge-write of the cache file has no lock, so concurrent resolves of the same module lose updates. Use `flock` or a per-process temp file with a merge step.
27. **\[BUG\] Hook.cpp:143-150.** `static bool inited` is checked and `GlossInit(false)` runs before the mutex is taken. Two threads can initialise twice. Use `std::call_once`.
28. **\[BUG, latent\] Hook.cpp:230-268.** `unhook`/`unhookAll` destroy `HookData`, whose destructor runs `GlossHookDelete` and restores bytes while a game thread may be inside the detour or trampoline. Keep trampolines alive (leak them) or quiesce first.
29. **\[BUG, latent\] Hook.cpp:67-89.** `rebuildChain` rewrites every `*originalFunc` pointer and calls `GlossHookReplaceNewFunc` while game threads are running the chain. Use atomic stores and release/acquire pairing.
30. **\[BUG\] CallbackSnapshot.hpp:51-53,92.** `std::atomic_load` on a `shared_ptr` is not a plain atomic load; libc++ implements it with an internal mutex plus a refcount bump. InputBridge.cpp:20 claims "one atomic load", and the deprecation warning is suppressed. Use `std::atomic&lt;const List*&gt;` and never free replaced lists (registration is rare).
31. **\[BUG\] InputBridge.cpp:202-203.** `catch (...) {}` in `DispatchDocumentResult` swallows a throwing callback silently. Log it once with `OnceReport`, as the other dispatchers do.
32. **\[BUG\] Signature.cpp:631-633.** A failed resolve (`0`) is stored in `sigCache` for the life of the process. PreLoader.cpp:85-90 documents that early resolution sees a partially mapped `libminecraftpe.so`, so one early miss is cached and the later correct attempt returns 0. Do not memoise misses.


## B. Hot-path and startup cost (33-80)


33. **\[PERF\] Signature.cpp:312.** `ModuleInfo cached = it-&gt;second;` deep-copies three vectors and a string on every lookup. Return `std::shared_ptr&lt;const ModuleInfo&gt;` instead.
34. **\[PERF\] Signature.cpp:104-113.** `RegionsAreMapped` issues one `process_vm_readv` per region on every lookup. Validate at most once per N ms, or key off a loader generation counter.
35. **\[PERF\] Signature.cpp:658-665.** `isExecutableAddress` re-fetches and copies the module on every call, and `hook()` callers use it. Cache the region list sorted and binary-search it.
36. **\[PERF\] Signature.cpp:604.** `ResolveExportedSymbol` runs `dlopen`+`dlsym`+`dlclose` for every pending signature, including hex byte patterns that can never be symbols. Skip it when the string contains a space or `?`.
37. **\[PERF\] Signature.cpp:587 and :279.** The `.sigcache` file is read and parsed twice per resolve (apply, then update). Parse once per module and keep the map in memory.
38. **\[PERF\] Signature.cpp:238,281.** Reading via `istreambuf_iterator&lt;char&gt;` is byte-by-byte. Use one `read()`/`pread()` into a pre-sized buffer.
39. **\[PERF\] Signature.cpp:328-339.** `getCachedPattern` returns `ParsedPattern` by value (copies its vectors) under a shared lock. Return `shared_ptr&lt;const ParsedPattern&gt;`.
40. **\[PERF\] Signature.cpp:358.** `selectAnchor` is re-run on a fresh copy every call. Cache the anchored pattern.
41. **\[PERF\] Signature.cpp:66-72.** `AnchorNode` is a 1 KB `next` array plus a `vector`. Flatten to one contiguous `uint32_t next[states*256]` table so the hot loop touches one cache line per byte, not two.
42. **\[PERF\] Signature.cpp:516.** The scan loop reads `nodes[state].outputs` (a vector at offset \~1032) for every byte of \~220 MB. Encode "has output" in a bit of the next-state value and only then touch outputs.
43. **\[PERF\] Signature.cpp:523.** The `maskedPatterns` loop runs for every byte. Build a 256-bit first-byte mask per pattern, or prefer exact anchors, so the common byte skips it.
44. **\[PERF\] Signature.cpp:496-532.** The scan is single-threaded over \~220 MB. Split regions/windows across 2-4 threads (read-only automaton, one result slot per pattern). Measure before and after.
45. **\[PERF\] Signature.cpp:440.** `process_vm_readv` copies the entire `.text` through the kernel into a buffer. Consider scanning in place under a `SIGSEGV` guard (or keep `readv` but only for regions that fail a cheap probe). Measure.
46. **\[PERF\] Signature.cpp:514.** `unresolved != 0` is re-checked per byte in the loop condition. Check it per window and when a match is recorded.
47. **\[PERF\] Signature.cpp:494.** `std::vector&lt;uint8_t&gt; buffer(kWindowBytes)` zero-fills 1 MB on every scan. Use an uninitialised buffer (`unique_ptr&lt;uint8_t[]&gt;(new uint8_t[n])`) or a reusable one.
48. **\[PERF\] Signature.cpp:126-163.** `getModuleInfo` parses every line of `/proc/self/maps` with `fgets`. For modules already loaded, `dl_iterate_phdr` returns the segments with no text parsing.
49. **\[PERF\] HookTarget.cpp:73-96.** `queryMemoryRegion` opens and parses all of `/proc/self/maps` per call. Reuse the module region cache or a short-TTL snapshot.
50. **\[PERF\] Hook.cpp:114 and :216.** `queryMemoryRegion` runs twice per hook install, plus `describe()` at :135. With about 15 hooks, that is 30+ full map parses at startup. Query once and reuse.
51. **\[PERF\] Hook.cpp:135,216.** `region.describe()` is evaluated as a log argument before the level check, so the string is built even when the log is disabled. Pass a lazily-evaluated value or guard with a level check.
52. **\[PERF\] Hook.cpp:147.** `GlossEnableLog(true)` is unconditional, so the backend logs every install in release builds. Enable it only in debug.
53. **\[PERF\] GamePlayerRender.cpp:85-95,119,136.** Two `clock_gettime` calls (`MonotonicMs` then `MonotonicUs`) per detour call. Read the clock once and derive milliseconds from microseconds.
54. **\[PERF\] FramePacing.hpp:127-132.** `onFrame` calls `reading()` on every render call, which sums 60 entries each time even when the 3 ms floor discarded the sample. Return early on a discarded sample and keep a running sum.
55. **\[PERF\] GamePlayerRender.cpp:137-142.** Four relaxed atomic stores per call even when no new sample was recorded. Store only when a sample was accepted.
56. **\[PERF\] GamePlayerRender.cpp:146-155.** The snapshot is published on every player-model render call. Publish once per detected frame, so cost no longer scales with the number of visible players.
57. **\[PERF\] GamePlayerRender.cpp:51-57.** Hot counters written by the render thread and counters read by other threads share cache lines. Use `alignas(64)` and group by writer.
58. **\[PERF\] GamePlayerRender.cpp:269-275.** `ReadFrameSnapshot` allocates a `std::vector` on every call. Add a `read(std::span&lt;uint8_t&gt;)` overload that fills a caller buffer.
59. **\[PERF\] SnapshotChannel.hpp:60.** `buffer_` is a heap `std::vector`, and `length_` sits next to `sequence_`. Make it a fixed `std::array` template parameter, cache-line aligned.
60. **\[PERF\] GameLocalPlayer.cpp:54-57,87.** `getLocalPlayer` is called many times per frame and each call runs `clock_gettime` plus a seqlock publish. Publish at most once per \~8 ms, or use the frame counter from the render hook.
61. **\[PERF\] GameLocalPlayer.cpp:72-89.** Skip the publish when position and rotation are bit-identical to the last one. This avoids bumping the sequence for nothing.
62. **\[PERF\] GameHooks.cpp `hook_isShowingMenu`.** It does an unconditional atomic store on every call. Use `if (load != res) store(res)` so the shared cache line is not dirtied.
63. **\[PERF\] InputBridge.cpp:144.** `std::string(text)` is allocated on every text event even when there are no C++ callbacks. Check for an empty list first.
64. **\[PERF\] InputBridge.cpp:94-112.** Touch-move events arrive at 120+ Hz and each builds an event struct and walks two lists. Add a fast path when both lists are empty.
65. **\[PERF\] InputBridge.cpp:98,109.** `consumed |= ...` keeps invoking callbacks after one consumed the event. Stop at the first consumer (or document why not).
66. **\[PERF\] JavaRuntime.cpp:109-115.** `CallActivityVoidMethod` does `GetObjectClass` + `GetMethodID` on every call. Cache the `jmethodID` (valid while the class is alive) after the first lookup.
67. **\[PERF\] JavaRuntime.cpp:139-156.** Clipboard access does 2 `FindClass` and 3 method lookups per call. Cache the class global refs and ids.
68. **\[PERF\] ExternalModBridgeJni.cpp:356,360,550.** `FindClass` on every call. Cache `java/lang/String` and `Object` global refs once.
69. **\[PERF\] OptifineProcess.cpp:23-28,50-70.** `FindThreadByName` opens an `ifstream` and builds a `std::string` for every thread of the process. Use `open/read/close` into a 16-byte stack buffer and stop at the first exact match.
70. **\[PERF\] OptifineProcess.cpp:17,52,63.** `Lower()` allocates a copy per thread. Compare case-insensitively without allocating.
71. **\[PERF\] OptifineProcess.cpp:104-125 and OptifineCpuAffinity.cpp:41.** The CPU frequency tables are re-read from sysfs on each retry. Compute once and cache.
72. **\[PERF\] OptifineMode.cpp:143-146.** `ReadOptifineState` copies a struct holding nine `std::string`s under the mutex per call. Return a compact snapshot with fixed-size fields.
73. **\[PERF\] OptifineMode.cpp:148-155.** `IsOptifineModeActive` takes a mutex to answer a boolean. Cache it in a `std::atomic&lt;bool&gt;`.
74. **\[PERF\] Patch.cpp:94,159,207.** Each patch does its own `mprotect` and cache flush. Group patches by page and protect/flush once per page.
75. **\[PERF\] Vtable.cpp:23.** The vtable-slot memo is in-memory only, so every launch re-walks `.data.rel.ro`. Persist RTTI-to-slot results in the same build-id-keyed cache file.
76. **\[PERF\] Vtable.cpp:98,138.** Each `resolveVtableFunction` call scans `.data.rel.ro` word by word for its typeinfo pointer. Build one index (typeinfo to vtable) per module in a single pass and share it.
77. **\[PERF\] PreLoader.cpp:145-152.** The self-test installs and removes every hook once "on the loading path before the real install", so the game is patched twice at launch. Run it on demand from diagnostics only.
78. **\[PERF\] GamePlayerRender.cpp:187-203.** Post-render callbacks run on every player-model call and rely on each callee to dedupe. Run them once per frame (after item 1 is fixed).
79. **\[PERF\] GamePlayerRender.cpp:205.** `DispatchRenderCallbacks()` has the same per-call problem. Dispatch once per frame.
80. **\[PERF\] OptifineEntityCulling.cpp:46, OptifineParticleCulling.cpp:38, OptifineOreUiStripping.cpp:38, OptifineCallbackTrimming.cpp:39.** `fetch_add` on every call (entity render runs per entity per frame) for a counter nothing consumes. Ship these disabled, and if kept use a single-writer `load`+`store`, which avoids the LL/SC loop.


## C. Build and link (81-110)


81. **\[BUILD\] CMakeLists.txt:\~(compile options).** Gradle passes no build type, so only `-O2` applies and the `-O3` branch never fires. Add `if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE) set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release)` before the target.
82. **\[BUILD\] Compile options.** Add `-DNDEBUG` explicitly. Without it, asserts in fmt, nlohmann and lunasvg stay on in a default build.
83. **\[BUILD\] Compile+link options.** Add `-flto=thin`. It inlines across translation units (Logger, CallbackSnapshot, SnapshotChannel, the dispatchers).
84. **\[BUILD\] Link options.** Add `-Wl,--icf=safe`. The four near-identical Optifine detours and fmt instantiations fold together, shrinking the mapped image.
85. **\[BUILD\] Link options.** Add `-Wl,--exclude-libs,ALL`. Static fmt and lunasvg symbols currently risk clashing with the game's or a mod's copies, and a smaller dynsym loads faster.
86. **\[BUILD\] Link options.** Add `-Wl,--pack-dyn-relocs=android`. It shrinks relocations and speeds `dlopen` on the 28+ API range this targets.
87. **\[BUILD\] Per-file flags.** Set `-O3` on hot files (`Signature.cpp`, `GamePlayerRender.cpp`, `InputBridge.cpp`, `GameLocalPlayer.cpp`) through `set_source_files_properties`.
88. **\[BUILD\] Per-file flags.** Set `-Oz` on cold files (`ModMenuBridge.cpp`, `ExternalModBridgeJni.cpp`, `ModManifest*.cpp`, `AntEggLoader.cpp`) to cut page-ins at load.
89. **\[BUILD\] PGO.** Collect a profile from a real launch (scan, hooks, one minute of play) and build with `-fprofile-use`. The scanner and dispatch loops benefit most.
90. **\[BUILD\] Do not add `-ffast-math`.** `FinitePosition` (GameLocalPlayer.cpp:65) relies on `std::isfinite`, which fast-math may fold away. If ever enabled, apply it per file and not here.
91. **\[BUILD\] Release artifacts.** Strip with `-Wl,--strip-all` and ship the unstripped `.so` as a symbol file for tombstone symbolication.
92. **\[BUILD\] Link options.** Add a `--version-script` exporting only `PL_EXPORT`, `JNI_OnLoad`, `Java_*` and the legacy C entry points.
93. **\[BUILD\] Link options.** Add `-Wl,--no-undefined` so a missing symbol fails at link time, not at `dlopen` on a user's phone.
94. **\[BUILD\] Compile time.** `target_precompile_headers` for `&lt;fmt/format.h&gt;`, `&lt;nlohmann/json.hpp&gt;` and the standard headers included in most files.
95. **\[BUILD\] CI.** Use `ccache` as the compiler launcher.
96. **\[BUILD\] Warnings.** No warning flags are set. Add `-Wall -Wextra -Werror=return-type -Werror=format`; a missing return in a passthrough detour is exactly the class that bites.
97. **\[BUILD\] Tests.** Add a ThreadSanitizer variant to `tests/cosmetics/run_tests.sh` so items 2-10 and 30 are caught by CI.
98. **\[BUILD\] Tests.** Add ASan+UBSan variants for the parser and pattern fuzz tests.
99. **\[BUILD\] FetchContent.** Five dependencies are cloned at configure time. Vendor them under `third_party/` so builds need no network and are faster.
100. **\[BUILD\] CMakeLists.txt `fmt::fmt` PUBLIC.** The public `Logger.hpp` includes fmt, forcing every mod to build against it. Hide fmt behind a non-template `vlog(level, string_view, fmt::format_args)` and drop the PUBLIC link; this also stabilises the ABI.
101. **\[BUILD\] lunasvg.** It is linked statically only to rasterise icons (ModMenuBridge.cpp:426). Measure its size contribution; if it is large, load it lazily or pre-render the icons at build time.
102. **\[BUILD\] Atomics.** Check that the NDK in use emits `-moutline-atomics` (or build with `-march=armv8.2-a+lse` for a device-class build); `fetch_add` on the hot counters otherwise compiles to LL/SC loops.
103. **\[BUILD\] STL.** The CMake file does not set `ANDROID_STL`; confirm what the Gradle module uses (static vs shared libc++). Two copies of libc++ in the process doubles startup work and breaks ODR assumptions.
104. **\[BUILD\] RTTI.** Try `-fno-rtti` (the code resolves game RTTI by name but does not appear to use `dynamic_cast`) and measure the size win. Unverified.
105. **\[BUILD\] CI.** Add `-Wl,--print-gc-sections` once to audit what `--gc-sections` is and is not removing.
106. **\[BUILD\] Reproducibility.** Add `-ffile-prefix-map=${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}=.` so builds are identical across machines.
107. **\[BUG\] CMakeLists.txt (install).** `install(DIRECTORY include/pl ... PATTERN "*.hpp")` skips the public `.h` headers (`BerryApiBridge.h`, `GameCosmetics.h`). Anything installing the SDK ships an incomplete header set. Add `PATTERN "*.h"`.
108. **\[BUILD\] CI guard.** AGENTS.md notes a `.cpp` not added to `PRELOADER_SOURCES` silently does not build. Add a CI check that globs `src/**/*.cpp` against the list. (I checked: every listed file exists today.)
109. **\[BUILD\] lib/ARM64/libGlossHook.a.** A 297 KB prebuilt archive with no version or hash recorded. Record the source commit and a SHA-256 in NOTICE, and build it from source with LTO if the licence allows.
110. **\[BUILD\] minSdk 28.** The comment in OptifineAllocator.cpp says minSdk 28 uses emulated TLS. Raising to API 29 gives native ELF TLS, which speeds `thread_local t_attachment` (JavaRuntime.cpp:36) and removes the malloc-in-TLS hazard documented there.


## D. Real FPS work (111-160)


Everything here is a hypothesis. It needs reverse engineering, a device, and the measurement harness from item 149 before any percentage is claimed.


111. **\[FPS\] New hook: `eglSwapBuffers` / `eglSwapBuffersWithDamage`.** FramePacing.hpp says the swap call "is not exposed by the stripped binary", but it is an exported libEGL symbol. Hooking it gives the true frame boundary and frame time, which every other item here needs.
112. **\[FPS\] New hook: `vkQueuePresentKHR`.** Same as 111 for a Vulkan path, if the build uses one.
113. **\[FPS\]** Drive `g_renderTick` and frame pacing from the swap hook instead of the per-player render call. This also repairs the cosmetics clock (item 1) at its root.
114. **\[FPS\]** Use `AChoreographer` and `eglSwapInterval` from native to align frame submission with the display period.
115. **\[FPS\]** Capture the game's window at `eglCreateWindowSurface` and call `ANativeWindow_setFrameRate` (or `ASurfaceTransaction_setFrameRate`, API 30) natively. OptifineRefreshRate.cpp:11-14 says only the launcher can do this today.
116. **\[FPS\]** Create an `APerformanceHint` session (API 33) for the render and main tids and report actual frame duration each frame. This is the supported replacement for `SCHED_FIFO`, which unprivileged apps are usually refused.
117. **\[FPS\]** Feed `AThermal_getThermalHeadroom` (API 30) into the governor so quality drops before the SoC throttles, not after.
118. **\[FPS\]** Feed the governor the real frame time from item 111. OptifineCallbackTrimming.cpp:18-21 uses an `AppPlatformListener` tick count as "FPS", which need not be one per frame.
119. **\[FPS\]** Find the render-distance setter with `resolveVtableSlotReferencingString` on the options string (for example `gfx_viewdistance`). The resolver already exists, and OptifineRenderDistance.cpp:15-21 says the missing setter is the only blocker.
120. **\[FPS\]** Same technique for particle distance and simulation distance options, so the governor has more than one knob.
121. **\[FPS\]** Dynamic resolution scale: locate the render-scale setting and let the governor lower it on GPU-bound frames.
122. **\[FPS\]** Entity distance culling. The Actor position offset `0x230` is already verified (GameLocalPlayer.cpp:21), so `EntityRenderDetour` can read the entity position and compare it to the local-player snapshot. The open question is which register holds the Actor; find it by disassembly.

```cpp
class PlayerSnapshot {
public:
  struct Data {
    float position[3];
    float rotation[2];
    long long stampMs;
  };

  void publish(const Data&amp; in) {
    const std::uint32_t start = seq_.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
    seq_.store(start + 1, std::memory_order_release);
    std::atomic_thread_fence(std::memory_order_release);
    for (int i=0;i&lt;3;++i) position_[i].store(in.position[i], relaxed);
    for (int i=0;i&lt;2;++i) rotation_[i].store(in.rotation[i], relaxed);
    stampMs_.store(in.stampMs, relaxed);
    seq_.store(start + 2, std::memory_order_release);
  }

  bool read(Data&amp; out) const {
    for (int attempt = 0; attempt &lt; kMaxRetries; ++attempt) {
      const std::uint32_t before = seq_.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
      if ((before &amp; 1u) != 0u) continue;      // retry rather than report "no player"
      if (before == 0) return false;          // never published
      Data d;
      for (...) d.position[i] = position_[i].load(relaxed);

      std::atomic_thread_fence(std::memory_order_acquire);

      if (before == after) { out = d; return true; }
    }
    return false;
  }
};
```

````text
Fix the frame-pacing window span and its shared scratch race

Three defects in FramePacingAnalyzer:

- The span used to normalise hitches-per-minute was the time since the
  first sample ever taken, so it grew for the life of the session while
  the window held only the last 2000 samples. A burst late in a long
  session was diluted: 100 hitches measured ~1500/min instead of ~2069/min.
  Each sample now carries its timestamp, so the span is the true span of
  the samples still in the ring.
- percentiles() sorted into one shared mutable scratch buffer, so two
  concurrent readers corrupted each other. The scratch is now guarded by a
  mutex that the render thread never takes, so a diagnostics read cannot
  stall a frame.
- percentiles() read the percentile ring while the render thread wrote it.
  The ring and the count/span it publishes are now relaxed atomics, and the
  copy is taken under the same mutex.

FramePacingTest gains a span case that measures 2069/min on this code and
1500/min on the old (bound 1800), and a two-thread case that must agree on
the median.
EOF
git log --oneline -3`
````

```cpp
void HookRender(void *a, void *b, void *c, void *d, void *e, void *f, void *g, void *h) {
  // One clock read per call. The millisecond value the snapshot carries is derived from it, so the
  // detour does not pay a second clock_gettime (audit item 53).
  const long long nowUs = MonotonicUs();
  const long long nowMs = nowUs / 1000;

  // Infer the frame boundary. The entry runs once per rendered player model, so several calls can
  // fall inside one frame; a 3ms floor collapses them to a single tick while still advancing every
  // real frame (the previous &gt;1s rule left the tick frozen during play — audit item 1).
  const bool newFrame = g_frameClock.onRenderCall(nowUs);
  if (newFrame) {
    g_frameCalls.store(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    g_renderTick.store(g_frameClock.tick(), std::memory_order_relaxed);
  } else {
    g_frameCalls.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
  }
  g_totalCalls.fetch_add(1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
  g_lastRenderMs.store(nowMs, std::memory_order_relaxed);

  // Feed the frame-time analyzer. The same timestamp is reused.

    const pl::render::FramePacingReading pacing =
        g_framePacing.onFrame(nowUs, g_displayRefreshHz.load(std::memory_order_relaxed), 3000);
```

````text
import json,subprocess,os
body = """## What this changes

Four correctness fixes in the render/UI data hand-off, each with a host test that fails against the
old code and passes against the new. No behaviour change for a healthy frame; the point is that the
seqlocks are now well-defined on ARM64 and the render tick actually advances during play.

This is **PR 1 of 3** for the preloader. PR 2 (build/link hardening + hot-path perf) and PR 3 (real
FPS work behind a benchmark harness) follow. Merge this one first.

### 1. Snapshot channel seqlock (items 2-4)

`publish` and `read` copied the payload with a plain `memcpy` on both sides. That is a data race even
when the sequence check discards the result, and a release store does not stop the following `memcpy`
from being ordered before it on ARM64, so a reader could see a half-written payload with an even
sequence.

- `publish`: release fence after the odd sequence store.
- `read`: acquire fence before re-reading the sequence.
- both: copy through `std::atomic_ref` relaxed, 8-byte words while both pointers are aligned and
  byte-wise otherwise.

Evidence: `SnapshotChannelTsanTest` reports the race at `SnapshotChannel.hpp:98` vs `:75` against the
old code and none against this one.

### 2. Local-player seqlock, extracted (items 5-7, 162)

`GameLocalPlayer.cpp` kept the transform in plain `float` arrays beside the counter: a race on every
field, the `acq_rel` acquire half did not keep the later plain stores after the store half, and a read
that landed in a write window returned "no player" instead of retrying.

- new `pl::ipc::PlayerSnapshot`: `std::atomic<float>` fields, release/acquire fences, retry budget.
- `GameLocalPlayer.cpp` publishes and reads through it.

Evidence: `PlayerSnapshotTsanTest` reports **5 races** against the old shape and none against this
one; `PlayerSnapshotTest` pins never-published / round-trip / latest-wins / no-torn-transform.

### 3. Frame-pacing window span + scratch race (items 8-10)

- The span used to normalise hitches-per-minute grew for the life of the session while the window held
  2000 samples, so a late burst was diluted: **1500/min measured instead of 2069/min**. Each sample now
  carries its timestamp, so the span is the ring's true span.
- `percentiles()` sorted into one shared mutable scratch buffer (two concurrent readers corrupt each
  other) and read the ring while the render thread wrote it. The scratch is now mutex-guarded (the
  render thread never takes it) and the ring is relaxed atomics.

Evidence: the new span case measures 2069/min here and 1500/min on the old header (bound 1800).

### 4. Render tick was frozen during play (item 1)

The "new frame" test was a gap of more than one second, but the render entry runs every ~16ms, so the
tick stayed at 1 for the whole session — cape/pet physics and the cosmetics frame version were starved.

- new `pl::render::FrameTickClock`: a 3ms floor collapses several model draws per frame into one tick
  and advances every real frame; a backwards timestamp starts a new frame.
- `HookRender` drives the tick from it and reads the clock once per call instead of two
````

````text
     8	// A scratch big enough for kOptifineMaxCores entries, so the helpers can sort a copy without
     9	// allocating (they are called from the apply pass, which must not allocate).
    10	constexpr int kScratch = kOptifineMaxCores;
    11	
    12	// Sorts @p values descending into @p out (which must hold @p count entries) and returns the number
    13	// of non-zero entries.
    14	int SortedDescending(const std::uint64_t *values, int count, std::uint64_t *out) {
    15	  int n = 0;
    16	  for (int i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
    17	    if (values[i] != 0) out[n++] = values[i];
    18	  }
    19	  for (int i = 1; i < n; ++i) {
    20	    const std::uint64_t key = out[i];
    21	    int j = i - 1;
    22	    while (j >= 0 && out[j] < key) {
    23	      out[j + 1] = out[j];
    24	      --j;
    25	    }
    26	    out[j + 1] = key;
    27	  }
    28	  return n;
    29	}
    30	
    31	/**
    32	 * @brief The frequency below which a core is a little core, or 0 when there is no gap to cluster on.
    33	 *
    34	 * The big cluster is the run of fastest cores up to the largest relative gap in the sorted table. A
    35	 * relative gap (a drop of at least kMinGapPercent of the higher value) is used rather than an absolute
    36	 * one so the rule is the same whether the table is in kHz or Hz.
    37	 */
    38	constexpr std::uint64_t kMinGapPercent = 8; // a >=8% drop separates two clusters
    39	
    40	std::uint64_t BigClusterThreshold(const std::uint64_t *sorted, int n) {
    41	  if (n <= 1) return 0;
    42	  std::uint64_t bestDrop = 0;
    43	  int bestIndex = -1; // the cluster boundary sits between bestIndex and bestIndex+1
    44	  for (int i = 0; i + 1 < n; ++i) {
    45	    const std::uint64_t high = sorted[i];
    46	    const std::uint64_t low = sorted[i + 1];
    47	    if (high == 0) continue;
    48	    const std::uint64_t drop = high - low;
    49	    if (drop * 100ULL < high * kMinGapPercent) continue; // not a cluster boundary
    50	    if (drop > bestDrop) {
    51	      bestDrop = drop;
    52	      bestIndex = i;
    53	    }
    54	  }
    55	  if (bestIndex < 0) return 0; // every core within kMinGapPercent of its neighbour: one cluster
    56	  return sorted[bestIndex + 1]; // the big cluster is everything at or above this
    57	}
    58	
    59	} // namespace
    60	
    61	int CountPerformanceCores(const std::uint64_t *maxFreqKhz, int count) {
    62	  if (maxFreqKhz == nullptr || count <= 0) return 0;
    63	
    64	  std::uint64_t fastest = 0;
    65	  for (int i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
    66	    if (maxFreqKhz[i] > fastest) fastest = maxFreqKhz[i];
    67	  }
    68	  // No core reported a frequency: the caller cannot tell fast from slow, so it must not pin.
    69	  if (fastest == 0) return 0;
    70	
    71	  int performance = 0;
    72	  for (int i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
    73	    if (maxFreqKhz[i] == 0) continue;
    74	    // Compare as integers to avoid floating-point edge cases: freq*10 >= fastest*9 is the
    75	    // same as freq/fastest >= 0.9, with no rounding surprises at exactly 0.9.
    76	    if (maxFreqKhz[i] * 10ULL >= fastest * 9ULL) ++performance;
    77	  }
    78	  return performance;
    79	}
    80	
    81	int BigClusterCoreCount(const std::uint64_t *maxFreqKhz, int count) {
    82	  if (maxFreqKhz == nullptr || count <= 0) return 0;
    83	  std::uint64_t sorted[kScratch] = {};
    84	  const int n = SortedDescending(maxFreqKhz, count > kScratch ? kScratch : count, sorted);
    85	  if (n == 0) return 0;
    86	  const std::uint64_t threshold = BigClusterThreshold(sorted, n);
    87	  if (threshold == 0) return 0; // no gap: cannot tell which cluster is the big one
    88	  int big = 0;
    89	  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    90	    if (sorted[i] >= threshold) ++big;
    91	  }
    92	  return big;
    93	}
    94	
    95	int SelectBigClusterCoreIndices(const std::uint64_t *maxFreqKhz, int count, int *out, int maxOut) {
````

```cpp
#pragma once
#include &lt;atomic&gt;
namespace pl::runtime {
inline std::atomic&lt;long&gt;&amp; RenderThreadIdStorage() {
  static std::atomic&lt;long&gt; tid{0};
  return tid;
}
inline void SetRenderThreadId(long tid) { RenderThreadIdStorage().store(tid, std::memory_order_relaxed); }
inline long RenderThreadId() { return RenderThreadIdStorage().load(std::memory_order_relaxed); }
}
```
Then HookRender calls SetRenderThreadId(::gettid()). And OptifineRenderPriority prefers RenderThreadId() when &gt; 0.

````text
old='''void ApplyRenderPriority(bool enabled, OptifineItemState &state) {
  if (!enabled) return;
  if (gApplied && gRenderTid > 0) {
    MarkOptifineActive(state, "render thread SCHED_FIFO priority 1");
    return;
  }

  for (const char *name : kRenderThreadNames) {
    const pid_t tid = FindThreadByName(name);
    if (tid > 0) {
      gRenderTid = tid;
      TryApplyToThread(tid, state);
      return;
    }
  }

  // The render thread is created when the game starts drawing, which is after this first
  // pass. Report "deferred" so the launcher retries rather than claiming success.
  MarkOptifineSkipped(state, "waiting for the render thread to start");
}'''
new='''void ApplyRenderPriority(bool enabled, OptifineItemState &state) {
  if (!enabled) return;
  const pid_t cached = gRenderTid.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
  if (gApplied.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) && cached > 0) {
    // Revalidate the cached tid: the render thread can be recreated and the kernel can recycle a
    // tid, so a stale one must not be reported Active (audit item 13).
    bool stillRender = false;
    for (const char *name : kRenderThreadNames) {
      if (ThreadNameMatches(cached, name)) {
        stillRender = true;
        break;
      }
    }
    if (stillRender) {
      MarkOptifineActive(state, "render thread SCHED_FIFO priority 1");
      return;
    }
    gApplied.store(false, std::memory_order_relaxed);
    gRenderTid.store(-1, std::memory_order_relaxed);
  }

  for (const char *name : kRenderThreadNames) {
    const pid_t tid = FindThreadByName(name);
    if (tid > 0) {
      gRenderTid.store(tid, std::memory_order_relaxed);
      TryApplyToThread(tid, state);
      return;
    }
  }

  // The render thread is created when the game starts drawing, which is after this first
  // pass. Report "deferred" so the launcher retries rather than claiming success.
  MarkOptifineSkipped(state, "waiting for the render thread to start");
}'''
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,new,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)
print('ok')
````

<sub>2026-11-06T11:27:01.780Z</sub>

````text
Command: `cd /workspace/work/preloader && git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Fix the Optifine item defects: core selection, thread matching, atomics

- Core selection counted a core as "performance" only within 10% of the
  fastest. On a tri-cluster SoC whose gold cores run below 0.9 of the prime
  core (Snapdragon 8 Gen 1: 2.5GHz gold vs 3.0GHz prime) that counts one
  core, so the "need 4+" check refused and CPU pinning silently did nothing.
  BigClusterCoreCount finds the cluster by the largest relative gap instead,
  recovering the whole prime+gold cluster. OptifineDeviceRulesTest pins nine
  real SoC frequency tables and asserts the old rule under-counts.
- The core scan broke on the first core without a cpufreq directory, so one
  offline core truncated the list. It now iterates /sys/.../cpu/present.
- FindThreadByName matched a substring case-insensitively, so "Render" hit
  Android's HWUI "RenderThread" and the real-time boost could land on the
  wrong thread. It is an exact, case-insensitive match now.
- "Minecraft Render" is 16 characters, but a task's comm is capped at 15, so
  that name could never match. It is "MinecraftRend" now.
- The cached render tid was never revalidated, so a recreated render thread
  was still reported Active. It is re-checked by name before reporting.
- gRequestedHz, gRenderTid, gApplied, gAppliedMask were plain globals written
  and read across threads; they are atomics now.
- CPU affinity pinned whichever thread ran the apply pass and assumed it was
  the main thread. It now refuses unless gettid() == getpid().
- install() shipped only *.hpp, dropping the public C headers.
EOF
git log --oneline -1`
````

**Three findings worth flagging, because they're the kind of thing that silently ships broken:**

1. **`std::atomic_ref` does not exist in NDK 28's libc++.** My first cut of the seqlock fix compiled fine on the host and would have **failed the real APK build**. Fixed with `__atomic` builtins. This is why I insisted on the native build.
2. **The preloader exports 2,624 symbols, 145 of them JNI.** A naive `--version-script` (audit item 92) would break native mods, which resolve `pl::` symbols from the host at `dlopen`. I used `--exclude-libs,ALL` instead — removes the fmt/std leak, preserves all 145 JNI + 9 `pl_` + 126 `pl::` symbols.

````text
     * Builds the Compose menu and adds it over the View menu's container.
     *
     * <p>The Compose tree is the presentation; the View tree underneath stays inflated so the
     * backdrop capture, the bind dialog and the panels that are still Views keep working, and so a
     * Compose failure leaves a working menu rather than a blank window.
     */
    private void attachComposeMenu() {
        if (!useComposeMenu || overlayView == null) return;
        try {
            composeMenuState = org.chimeramc.client.ui.compose.modmenu.ModMenuHost.state(
                    org.chimeramc.client.ui.compose.modmenu.ModMenuStateBuilder.build(
                            allMods,

            composeMenuView = new androidx.compose.ui.platform.ComposeView(activity);
            composeMenuView.setLayoutParams(new FrameLayout.LayoutParams(
                    FrameLayout.LayoutParams.MATCH_PARENT,
                    FrameLayout.LayoutParams.MATCH_PARENT));

            org.chimeramc.client.ui.compose.modmenu.ModMenuHost.setContent(
                    composeMenuView,
                    composeMenuState,
                    destination -> {
                        if (composeMenuState == null) return;
                        composeMenuState.setValue(composeMenuState.getValue()
                                .copy(destination));
                    },
                    query -> {
                        if (composeMenuState == null) return;
                        composeMenuState.setValue(composeMenuState.getValue().copy(query, false,

                                current.getGlassTint(), current.getOpacityPercent()));
                    },
                    (key, enabled) -> onComposeSettingToggle(key, enabled),
                    this::hide);

            FrameLayout host = overlayView.findViewById(R.id.mod_menu_container);
            if (host != null) {
                host.addView(composeMenuView);
            } else {
                ((android.view.ViewGroup) overlayView).addView(composeMenuView);
            }
        } catch (Throwable e) {
            // Compose failing must never take the menu down: the View menu is already inflated
            // underneath, so dropping the Compose layer leaves a working screen.
            AppLog.warnOnce("GlowberryClient", "ModMenuOverlay:compose",
                    "The Compose Mod Menu could not start; using the View menu", e);
            composeMenuView = null;
            composeMenuState = null;
        }
    }

    /** Persists a module toggle from the Compose menu and refreshes the rows. */
    private void onComposeModuleToggle(String stableKey, boolean enabled) {
        for (UnifiedMod mod : allMods) {
            if (!org.chimeramc.client.ui.compose.modmenu.ModMenuStateBuilder
                    .matchesKey(mod, stableKey)) {
                continue;
            }
            boolean applied = org.chimeramc.client.ui.compose.modmenu.ModMenuStateBuilder
                    .toggle(mod, enabled);
            InbuiltModManager manager = InbuiltModManager.getInstance(activity);
            if (mod.getSource() == UnifiedMod.Source.INBUILT) {
                manager.setInbuiltModEnabled(mod.getModId(), applied);
            } else {
                manager.setExternalModuleEnabled(mod.getModId(), applied);
            }
            break;
        }
        refreshComposeMenu();
    }

    /** Persists a favorite toggle from the Compose menu. */
    private void onComposeFavoriteToggle(String stableKey) {
        boolean nowFavorite = !favoriteKeys.contains(stableKey);
        if (nowFavorite) {
            favoriteKeys.add(stableKey);
        } else {
            favoriteKeys.remove(stableKey);
        }
        InbuiltModManager.getInstance(activity).setModFavorite(stableKey, nowFavorite);
        refreshComposeMenu();
    }

    /** Applies a settings toggle from the Compose menu's Settings destination. */
    private void onComposeSettingToggle(String key, boolean enabled) {
        InbuiltModManager.getInstance(activity).setModConfigBool(key, enabled);
        refreshComposeMenu();
    }

    /** Rebuilds the Compose state from the mod list, preserving the destination and the filters. */
    private void refreshComposeMenu() {
        if (composeMenuState == null) return;
        var current = composeMenuState.getValue();
        var rebuilt = org.chimeramc.client.ui.compose.modmenu.ModMenuStateBuilder.build(
                allMods, favoriteKeys, current.getDestination());
        composeMenuState.setValue(rebuilt.copy(rebuilt.getDestination(), current.getSearch(),
                current.getFavoritesOnly(), current.getGlassTint(),
                current.getOpacityPercent()));
    }

    private void showFallback() {'''
````

````text
import sys, re

def parse(pattern):
````

Confirmed: index 3 never chosen. My rejection logic is wrong.

`choice = random.nextInt(count - 1)` gives [0, count-2]. For count=4: [0,2]. Then `if (choice &gt;= previous) choice += 1`.

With previous = -1: `previous &gt;= 0` is false, so choice stays [0,2] → **3 is never chosen**. Bug.

Also for previous &gt;= 0 the mapping isn't uniform.

Correct approach: draw uniformly from [0, count) and reject if it equals previous; retry. That's a rejection sampler — uniform over the allowed set, and termination is certain (at most a few retries).

```java
public static int pick(int count, int previous, Random random) {
    if (count &lt;= 0) return -1;
    if (count == 1) return 0;
    if (random == null) return (previous &gt;= 0 &amp;&amp; previous &lt; count) ? (previous + 1) % count : 0;
    boolean restrict = previous &gt;= 0 &amp;&amp; previous &lt; count;
    for (int attempt = 0; attempt &lt; 64; attempt++) {
        int choice = random.nextInt(count);
        if (!restrict || choice != previous) return choice;
    }
    // Vanishingly unlikely; fall back to the next index deterministically.
    return restrict ? (previous + 1) % count : 0;
}
```

This is uniform over [0,count) when previous is unknown, and uniform over the other count-1 values when known.

Note: I should apply the same fix to `pick(List,...)`. It delegates to `pick(int,...)` so it inherits the fix.

## PR-11: I did the verification, and it changes the answer

I downloaded all 7 APKs (3.6 GB), extracted each `libminecraftpe.so`, and scanned it with **the loader's own signature patterns**.

**"MB shader loader" = `mtbinloader2` (mbl2 v0.1.12)** — a Rust library, vendored as `libmtbinloader2.so`. It's not a renderer; it hooks `ResourcePackManager` + AAsset to load materialbins, and autofixes shaders by byte-signature. Support is *empirical* — it matches bytes, so the only real question is whether the pattern still hits.

| Version | ABI in APK | Pattern result | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **26.60** | arm64-v8a | `26.60` exact → **1 match** @ `0xcf8a670` | ✅ **works today** |
| **26.52** | arm64-v8a | `26.50` → **1 match** | ✅ **works today** |
| **26.51** | arm64-v8a | `26.50` → **1 match** | ✅ **works today** |
| **26.50** | arm64-v8a | `26.50` → **1 match** | ✅ **works today** |
| 26.45 / 26.44 / 26.40 | **armeabi-v7a only** | no arm64 binary exists | ❌ **cannot run here** |
| 26.41 | — | mcpe-planet returns 404 | doesn't exist |

**The headline: 26.50, 26.51, 26.52 and 26.60 already work — no code change needed.** The loader's `26.50` pattern covers 51 and 52 too; that's why it never named them.

**And 26.40/26.44/26.45 have no arm64 binary at all** — they're 32-bit-only builds, and this client is `abiFilters 'arm64-v8a'`. So those can't be launched here *regardless of the loader*. There's nothing to fix; the fix is "use the arm64 build." I wrote up the re-derivation procedure in `docs/agents/mb-shader-loader-version-support.md` for when a future build does break it.

## My own bug, caught by my own test

I wrote the splash background picker with `nextInt(count - 1)` and a shift past the previous index. That **can never return the last index** — one background would silently never appear. `SplashBackgroundsTest` failed on exactly that. Fixed with a rejection loop. That's the test-first rule earning its keep.

````text
    private void finishSequence() {
````

````text
### Splash: the 3D scene is gone

The splash drew a particle system, a terrain mesh, an animated pickaxe, a block-break sequence and a
wordmark shatter **every frame** on the cold-start path — for a screen the user looks at for about two
seconds. It is now:

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| floating island + particles (3D scene) | one still background image |
| ore block cracking in 6 stages | — |
| pickaxe swing, wind-up, arc travel | — |
| wordmark shatter + white circular wipe | a 220ms fade |
| — | **one smooth circle rotating in the bottom-right** |

- **8 backgrounds** from minecraft.net key art and wallpapers, installed as
  `drawable-nodpi/splash_bg_1..8`. A launch picks one uniformly and **never repeats the previous
  choice** (`SplashBackgroundRegistry` remembers the last index).
- `SplashSpinner` is one rotating arc on a hardware-accelerated canvas, driven by the view's own
  animation clock so it stops with the view instead of leaving a timer running.
- The warm-up stays **time-budgeted, not time-fixed**: `SplashTimeline` still computes
  `min(real, paced)`, so a fast start gets a watchable beat and a slow one holds rather than looping.
- The new completion always navigates — the old animator chain could strand the user on a frozen
  splash if an animator never ended, so the fade has a handler backstop.

The Minecraft Usage Guidelines require a disclaimer on related materials that use Mojang's assets,
so the splash renders, verbatim:

using the key art legitimate rather than merely tolerated.

The compatibility card rendered *inside the wizard's install step*, so the setup flow carried a
````

````text
package org.chimeramc.client.launcher.core.auth;

import static org.junit.Assert.assertFalse;
import static org.junit.Assert.assertTrue;

import org.junit.Test;

/**
 * The rule that decides when a stored sign-in snapshot must be refreshed before a launch.
 *
 * <p>This is the rule whose absence caused "signed in, but the game starts signed out, so sign in
 * again": the serialised chain is a snapshot with its own expiries, and reading it back renews
 * nothing.
 */
public class AccountTokenFreshnessTest {

    private static final long NOW = 1_700_000_000_000L;
    private static final long HOUR = 60L * 60L * 1000L;

    @Test
    public void materialWrittenJustNowIsNotRefreshed() {
        assertFalse(AccountTokenFreshness.shouldRefresh(NOW, NOW));
        assertFalse(AccountTokenFreshness.shouldRefresh(NOW - HOUR, NOW));
    }

    @Test
    public void materialOlderThanTheTrustWindowIsRefreshed() {
        assertTrue(AccountTokenFreshness.shouldRefresh(
                NOW - AccountTokenFreshness.MAX_TRUST_MS, NOW));
        assertTrue(AccountTokenFreshness.shouldRefresh(NOW - 2 * AccountTokenFreshness.MAX_TRUST_MS, NOW));
    }

    @Test
    public void theBoundaryIsExactlyTheTrustWindow() {
        assertFalse(AccountTokenFreshness.shouldRefresh(
                NOW - AccountTokenFreshness.MAX_TRUST_MS + 1, NOW));
        assertTrue(AccountTokenFreshness.shouldRefresh(
                NOW - AccountTokenFreshness.MAX_TRUST_MS, NOW));
    }

    @Test
    public void anUnstampedEntryIsAlwaysRefreshed() {
        // 0 is what a record written before the stamp existed carries, and what a corrupt read
        // yields. It cannot be trusted, so it is refreshed once.
        assertTrue(AccountTokenFreshness.shouldRefresh(0, NOW));
        assertTrue(AccountTokenFreshness.shouldRefresh(-5, NOW));
    }

    @Test
    public void aBackwardsClockDoesNotForceARefreshLoop() {
        // The wall clock moved back (a manual change, or a timezone bug). Refreshing on every call
        // would be a network call per launch forever; keeping the material is the safer failure.
        assertFalse(AccountTokenFreshness.shouldRefresh(NOW, NOW - 10 * HOUR));
    }

    @Test
    public void aNonsenseNowDoesNotForceARefresh() {
        assertFalse(AccountTokenFreshness.shouldRefresh(NOW, 0));
    }

    @Test
    public void usableMaterialMustBeNonEmptyJson() {
        assertTrue(AccountTokenFreshness.hasUsableMaterial("{\"msaToken\":{}}"));
        assertTrue(AccountTokenFreshness.hasUsableMaterial("  {\"a\":1}  "));
        assertFalse(AccountTokenFreshness.hasUsableMaterial(null));
        assertFalse(AccountTokenFreshness.hasUsableMaterial(""));
        assertFalse(AccountTokenFreshness.hasUsableMaterial("   "));
        assertFalse(AccountTokenFreshness.hasUsableMaterial("not-json"));
    }
}
EOF
````

````text
new = '''    /**
     * Refreshes a stored account's sign-in material and writes the renewed chain back.
     *
     * <p><b>Why this exists.</b> A serialised {@code BedrockAuthManager} is a snapshot of the whole
     * token chain (MSA, XBL, XSTS, the Minecraft certificate), and every step in it has its own
     * expiry. Reading the snapshot back does <em>not</em> renew anything, so an account signed in a
     * day or two ago holds an expired certificate. Exporting that snapshot as-is gives the game a
     * sign-in it rejects, which is why a user who was already signed in kept being asked to sign in
     * again. {@link BedrockAuthManager#fromJson} plus {@code getUpToDate()} on each step is what
     * actually renews, and the renewed chain is what gets serialised back.
     *
     * <p>Best-effort by contract: a failure returns false and leaves the stored material untouched,
     * so a launch with no network still exports the previous chain rather than nothing. That is the
     * same fail-open choice {@code XalExporter} already makes.
     *
     * @return true when the stored chain was refreshed and rewritten.
     */
    public static boolean refreshStoredAccount(Context context, MsftAccountStore.MsftAccount account) {
        if (context == null || account == null) return false;
        if (!AccountTokenFreshness.hasUsableMaterial(account.serializedAuthManager)) return false;
        try {
            HttpClient httpClient = createHttpClient();
            JsonObject json = JsonParser.parseString(account.serializedAuthManager).getAsJsonObject();
            BedrockAuthManager authManager = BedrockAuthManager.fromJson(httpClient, GAME_VERSION, json);

            // Touch every step so each renews if it is near expiry, then serialise the result. The
            // certificate chain is the one the game validates, so it is the last to be pulled.
            authManager.getMsaToken().getUpToDate();
            authManager.getXboxLiveToken().getUpToDate();
            authManager.getXboxLiveXstsToken().getUpToDate();
            authManager.getMinecraftCertificateChain().getUpToDate();

            JsonObject refreshed = authManager.toJson().getAsJsonObject();
            MsftAccountStore.updateAuthMaterial(context, account.id, refreshed.toString());
            return true;
        } catch (Throwable t) {
            Log.w(TAG, "Could not refresh the stored sign-in material", t);
            return false;
        }
    }

    public static String[] xboxLiveXsts(MsftAccountStore.MsftAccount account) {'''
````

````text
     *
     * <p>The stamp is what {@code AccountTokenFreshness} reads, so a renewed chain is not renewed

    public static synchronized void updateAuthMaterial(Context ctx, String id, String serialized) {
        if (id == null || serialized == null) return;
        List<MsftAccount> accounts = list(ctx);
        boolean changed = false;
        for (MsftAccount a : accounts) {
            if (id.equals(a.id)) {
                a.serializedAuthManager = serialized;
                a.lastUpdated = System.currentTimeMillis();
                changed = true;
            }
        }
        if (changed) save(ctx, accounts);
    }
````

I've hit my three-strike limit on this build error, so per your stop-loss rule I'm stopping and reporting rather than guessing further.

**I did find and fix three real bugs in the sign-in path first** — that work is real and testable:

### Bug 1 — MSAL uses a placeholder client ID
`MsftLoginActivity` hardcodes `YOUR_CLIENT_ID_HERE` in **two** places (lines ~215 and ~245). That button — labelled **"Microsoft OAuth (Official)"** — can never work. The device-code and WebView paths use the real `MsaConstants.BEDROCK_ANDROID_TITLE_ID`; MSAL was never given one.

### Bug 2 — MSAL never produces a playable session
`completeMsalLogin()` only returns a **username** and calls `finish()`. It never runs the XBL → XSTS → Minecraft-certificate chain that `MsftAuthManager.loginWithCode()` does. So even with a valid client ID, MSAL would "succeed" and the game would still launch signed out.

### Bug 3 — nothing ever refreshes the stored token ← *this is your actual symptom*
A serialized `BedrockAuthManager` is a **snapshot**; `BedrockAuthManager.fromJson()` does not renew anything. `XalExporter` writes that snapshot into the game's XAL directory at launch. So an account signed in a day ago exports an **expired certificate**, and the game starts signed out — which is exactly why you "constantly click sign in."

I added `AccountTokenFreshness` (pure, 7 tests written) and `MsftAuthManager.refreshStoredAccount()` that does `fromJson` → `getUpToDate()` on each step → `BedrockAuthManager.toJson()` → writes back.

````text
import static org.junit.Assert.assertFalse;
import static org.junit.Assert.assertTrue;

import org.junit.Test;

/**
 * The sign-in freshness rule in {@link MsftAuthManager}.
 *
 * <p>This is the rule whose absence caused "signed in, but the game starts signed out, so sign in
 * again": a serialised chain is a snapshot with its own expiries, and reading it back renews
 * nothing, so an old snapshot exported at launch is an expired sign-in.
 */
public class MsftAuthManagerFreshnessTest {

    private static final long NOW = 1_700_000_000_000L;
    private static final long HOUR = 60L * 60L * 1000L;

    @Test
    public void materialWrittenJustNowIsNotRefreshed() {
        assertFalse(MsftAuthManager.shouldRefreshTokens(NOW, NOW));
        assertFalse(MsftAuthManager.shouldRefreshTokens(NOW - HOUR, NOW));
    }

    @Test
    public void materialOlderThanTheTrustWindowIsRefreshed() {
        assertTrue(MsftAuthManager.shouldRefreshTokens(
                NOW - MsftAuthManager.TOKEN_MAX_TRUST_MS, NOW));
        assertTrue(MsftAuthManager.shouldRefreshTokens(
                NOW - 2 * MsftAuthManager.TOKEN_MAX_TRUST_MS, NOW));
    }

    @Test
    public void theBoundaryIsExactlyTheTrustWindow() {
        assertFalse(MsftAuthManager.shouldRefreshTokens(
                NOW - MsftAuthManager.TOKEN_MAX_TRUST_MS + 1, NOW));
        assertTrue(MsftAuthManager.shouldRefreshTokens(
                NOW - MsftAuthManager.TOKEN_MAX_TRUST_MS, NOW));
    }

    @Test
    public void anUnstampedEntryIsAlwaysRefreshed() {
        assertTrue(MsftAuthManager.shouldRefreshTokens(0, NOW));
        assertTrue(MsftAuthManager.shouldRefreshTokens(-5, NOW));
    }

    @Test
    public void aBackwardsClockDoesNotForceARefreshLoop() {
        assertFalse(MsftAuthManager.shouldRefreshTokens(NOW, NOW - 10 * HOUR));
    }

    @Test
    public void aNonsenseNowDoesNotForceARefresh() {
        assertFalse(MsftAuthManager.shouldRefreshTokens(NOW, 0));
    }

    @Test
    public void usableMaterialMustBeNonEmptyJson() {
        assertTrue(MsftAuthManager.hasUsableAuthMaterial("{\\"msaToken\\":{}}"));
        assertTrue(MsftAuthManager.hasUsableAuthMaterial("  {\\"a\\":1}  "));
        assertFalse(MsftAuthManager.hasUsableAuthMaterial(null));
        assertFalse(MsftAuthManager.hasUsableAuthMaterial(""));
        assertFalse(MsftAuthManager.hasUsableAuthMaterial("   "));
        assertFalse(MsftAuthManager.hasUsableAuthMaterial("not-json"));
    }
}
'''
````

````text
Command: `cd /workspace/project/GlowberryClient && cat > app/src/main/java/org/chimeramc/client/launcher/core/mods/inbuilt/overlay/ModMenuComposeHost.java <<'EOF'
package org.chimeramc.client.launcher.core.mods.inbuilt.overlay;

import android.app.Activity;
import android.view.View;
import android.view.ViewGroup;
import android.widget.FrameLayout;

import androidx.compose.runtime.MutableState;
import androidx.compose.ui.platform.ComposeView;

import org.chimeramc.client.R;
import org.chimeramc.client.core.mods.inbuilt.UnifiedMod;
import org.chimeramc.client.ui.compose.modmenu.ModMenuDestination;
import org.chimeramc.client.ui.compose.modmenu.ModMenuHost;
import org.chimeramc.client.ui.compose.modmenu.ModMenuState;
import org.chimeramc.client.ui.compose.modmenu.ModMenuStateBuilder;
import org.chimeramc.client.util.AppLog;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.Set;

/**
 * Hosts the Compose Mod Menu over the View menu's container.
 *
 * <p>Extracted from {@link ModMenuOverlay} so that class stays inside its size budget. The overlay
 * keeps the View tree, the persistence and the callbacks; this class owns the Compose view, its
 * state, and the mapping from Compose interactions back to the overlay's persistence.
 *
 * <p>The Compose tree is layered <em>over</em> the already-inflated View tree, so a Compose failure
 * is caught and logged here and the working View menu stays visible rather than a blank window.
 */
final class ModMenuComposeHost {

    /** Called when a module toggle arrives from the Compose UI. */
    interface ModuleToggle {
        void onToggle(String stableKey, boolean enabled);
    }

    private static final String TAG = "ModMenuComposeHost";

    private final Activity activity;
    private final View overlayView;
    private final List<UnifiedMod> mods;
    private final Set<String> favoriteKeys;
    private final ModuleToggle moduleToggle;
    private final Runnable onRowsChanged;
    private final Runnable onClose;

    private ComposeView composeView;
    private MutableState<ModMenuState> state;
    private boolean attached;

    ModMenuComposeHost(Activity activity,
                       View overlayView,
                       List<UnifiedMod> mods,
                       Set<String> favoriteKeys,
                       ModuleToggle moduleToggle,
                       Runnable onRowsChanged,
                       Runnable onClose) {
        this.activity = activity;
        this.overlayView = overlayView;
        this.mods = mods;
        this.favoriteKeys = favoriteKeys;
        this.moduleToggle = moduleToggle;
        this.onRowsChanged = onRowsChanged;
        this.onClose = onClose;
    }

    /** Builds the Compose menu and adds it over the View menu's container. Idempotent. */
    void attach() {
        if (attached || overlayView == null) return;
        attached = true;
        try {
            state = ModMenuHost.state(
                    ModMenuStateBuilder.build(mods, favoriteKeys, ModMenuDestination.MODULES));

            composeView = new ComposeView(activity);
            composeView.setLayoutParams(new FrameLayout.LayoutParams(
                    FrameLayout.LayoutParams.MATCH_PARENT,
                    FrameLayout.LayoutParams.MATCH_PARENT));

            ModMenuHost.setContent(
                    composeView,
                    state,
                    destination -> update(s -> s.withDestination(destination)),
                    query -> update(s -> s.withSearch(query)),
                    (stableKey, enabled) -> {
                        moduleToggle.onToggle(stableKey, enabled);
                        refresh();
                    },
                    stableKey -> {
                        toggleFavorite(stableKey);
                        refresh();
                    },
                    () -> update(s -> s.withFavoritesOnly(!s.getFavoritesOnly())),
                    (key, enabled) -> {
                        org.chimeramc.client.core.mods.inbuilt.manager.InbuiltModManager
                                .getInstance(activity).setModConfigBool(key, enabled);
                        refresh();
                    },
                    onClose::run);

            FrameLayout host = overlayView.findViewById(R.id.mod_menu_container);
            if (host != null) {
                host.addView(composeView);
            } else if (overlayView instanceof ViewGroup) {
                ((ViewGroup) overlayView).addView(composeView);
            }
        } catch (Throwable e) {
            // Compose failing must never take the menu down: the View menu is already inflated
            // underneath, so dropping the Compose layer leaves a working screen.
            AppLog.warnOnce("GlowberryClient", "ModMenuComposeHost:attach",
                    "The Compose Mod Menu could not start; using the View menu", e);
            composeView = null;
            state = null;
            attached = false;
        }
    }

    /** Rebuilds the rows from the current mod list, preserving the destination and the filters. */
    void refresh() {
        if (state == null) return;
        try {
            final ModMenuState current = state.getValue();
            final ModMenuState rebuilt =
                    ModMenuStateBuilder.build(mods, favoriteKeys, current.getDestination());
            state.setValue(rebuilt
                    .withSearch(current.getSearch())
                    .withFavoritesOnly(current.getFavoritesOnly()));
            if (onRowsChanged != null) onRowsChanged.run();
        } catch (Throwable e) {
            AppLog.warnOnce("GlowberryClient", "ModMenuComposeHost:refresh",
                    "Could not rebuild the Compose menu rows", e);
        }
    }

    private void update(java.util.function.UnaryOperator<ModMenuState> change) {
        if (state == null) return;
        state.setValue(change.apply(state.getValue()));
    }

    private void toggleFavorite(String stableKey) {
        if (stableKey == null) return;
        final boolean nowFavorite = !favoriteKeys.contains(stableKey);
        if (nowFavorite) {
            favoriteKeys.add(stableKey);
        } else {
            favoriteKeys.remove(stableKey);
        }
        org.chimeramc.client.core.mods.inbuilt.manager.InbuiltModManager
                .getInstance(activity).setModFavorite(stableKey, nowFavorite);
    }
}
EOF
````

````text
content = '''package org.chimeramc.client.core.mods.inbuilt.overlay;

import android.app.Activity;
import android.view.View;
import android.view.ViewGroup;
import android.widget.FrameLayout;

import androidx.compose.runtime.MutableState;
import androidx.compose.ui.platform.ComposeView;

import org.chimeramc.client.R;
import org.chimeramc.client.core.mods.inbuilt.UnifiedMod;
import org.chimeramc.client.core.mods.inbuilt.manager.InbuiltModManager;
import org.chimeramc.client.ui.compose.modmenu.ModMenuDestination;
import org.chimeramc.client.ui.compose.modmenu.ModMenuHost;
import org.chimeramc.client.ui.compose.modmenu.ModMenuState;
import org.chimeramc.client.ui.compose.modmenu.ModMenuStateBuilder;
import org.chimeramc.client.util.AppLog;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.Set;
import java.util.function.UnaryOperator;

/**
 * Hosts the Compose Mod Menu over the View menu's container.
 *
 * <p>Extracted from ModMenuOverlay so that class stays inside its size budget. The overlay keeps the
 * View tree, the persistence and the callbacks; this class owns the Compose view, its state, and the
 * mapping from Compose interactions back to the overlay's persistence.
 *
 * <p>The Compose tree is layered over the already-inflated View tree, so a Compose failure is caught
 * and logged here and the working View menu stays visible rather than a blank window.
 */
final class ModMenuComposeHost {

    /** Called when a module toggle arrives from the Compose UI. */
    interface ModuleToggle {
        void onToggle(String stableKey, boolean enabled);
    }

    private final Activity activity;
    private final View overlayView;
    private final List<UnifiedMod> mods;
    private final Set<String> favoriteKeys;
    private final ModuleToggle moduleToggle;
    private final Runnable onRowsChanged;
    private final Runnable onClose;

    private ComposeView composeView;
    private MutableState<ModMenuState> state;
    private boolean attached;

    ModMenuComposeHost(Activity activity,
                       View overlayView,
                       List<UnifiedMod> mods,
                       Set<String> favoriteKeys,
                       ModuleToggle moduleToggle,
                       Runnable onRowsChanged,
                       Runnable onClose) {
        this.activity = activity;
        this.overlayView = overlayView;
        this.mods = mods;
        this.favoriteKeys = favoriteKeys;
        this.moduleToggle = moduleToggle;
        this.onRowsChanged = onRowsChanged;
        this.onClose = onClose;
    }

    /** Builds the Compose menu and adds it over the View menu's container. Idempotent. */
    void attach() {
        if (attached || overlayView == null) return;
        attached = true;
        try {
            state = ModMenuHost.state(
                    ModMenuStateBuilder.build(mods, favoriteKeys, ModMenuDestination.MODULES));

            composeView = new ComposeView(activity);
            composeView.setLayoutParams(new FrameLayout.LayoutParams(
                    FrameLayout.LayoutParams.MATCH_PARENT,
                    FrameLayout.LayoutParams.MATCH_PARENT));

            ModMenuHost.setContent(
                    composeView,
                    state,
                    destination -> update(s -> s.withDestination(destination)),
                    query -> update(s -> s.withSearch(query)),
                    (stableKey, enabled) -> {
                        moduleToggle.onToggle(stableKey, enabled);
                        refresh();
                    },
                    stableKey -> {
                        toggleFavorite(stableKey);
                        refresh();
                    },
                    () -> update(s -> s.withFavoritesOnly(!s.getFavoritesOnly())),
                    (key, enabled) -> {
                        InbuiltModManager.getInstance(activity).setModConfigBool(key, enabled);
                        refresh();
                    },
                    onClose::run);

            FrameLayout host = overlayView.findViewById(R.id.mod_menu_container);
            if (host != null) {
                host.addView(composeView);
            } else if (overlayView instanceof ViewGroup) {
                ((ViewGroup) overlayView).addView(composeView);
            }
        } catch (Throwable e) {
            // Compose failing must never take the menu down: the View menu is already inflated
            // underneath, so dropping the Compose layer leaves a working screen.
            AppLog.warnOnce("GlowberryClient", "ModMenuComposeHost:attach",
                    "The Compose Mod Menu could not start; using the View menu", e);
            composeView = null;
            state = null;
            attached = false;
        }
    }

    /** Rebuilds the rows from the current mod list, preserving the destination and the filters. */
    void refresh() {
        if (state == null) return;
        try {
            final ModMenuState current = state.getValue();
            final ModMenuState rebuilt =
                    ModMenuStateBuilder.build(mods, favoriteKeys, current.getDestination());
            state.setValue(rebuilt
                    .withSearch(current.getSearch())
                    .withFavoritesOnly(current.getFavoritesOnly()));
            if (onRowsChanged != null) onRowsChanged.run();
        } catch (Throwable e) {
            AppLog.warnOnce("GlowberryClient", "ModMenuComposeHost:refresh",
                    "Could not rebuild the Compose menu rows", e);
        }
    }

    private void update(UnaryOperator<ModMenuState> change) {
        if (state == null) return;
        state.setValue(change.apply(state.getValue()));
    }

    private void toggleFavorite(String stableKey) {
        if (stableKey == null) return;
        final boolean nowFavorite = !favoriteKeys.contains(stableKey);
        if (nowFavorite) {
            favoriteKeys.add(stableKey);
        } else {
            favoriteKeys.remove(stableKey);
        }
        InbuiltModManager.getInstance(activity).setModFavorite(stableKey, nowFavorite);
    }
}
'''
````

````text
        assertFalse("a placeholder client id can never complete a sign-in",
                id.toUpperCase().contains("YOUR_CLIENT_ID"));
        assertFalse(id.trim().isEmpty());
        assertFalse("a placeholder marker leaked in", id.contains("HERE"));

        // MSA title ids are 16 hex characters. A UUID-style id here would be an Azure app
        // registration, which is a different thing and would not authenticate a Bedrock title.
        String id = MsftAuthManager.bedrockClientId();
        assertTrue("expected 16 hex chars, got: " + id, id.matches("[0-9a-fA-F]{16}"));
    }
}
````

`completeMsalLogin()` returned a **username** and called `finish()`. It never ran the Xbox Live → XSTS → certificate chain. So even with a valid client ID, the launcher said "signed in" while the game launched signed out — **the same visible symptom as the token bug, from a different cause.**

**MSAL doesn't expose a refresh token here**, so a chain built from MSAL sign-in can't renew itself. Device-code stays the renewing path — which is exactly what your labels already say.
