import android.app.Activity;
import android.view.View;
import android.view.ViewGroup;
import android.widget.FrameLayout;

import androidx.compose.runtime.MutableState;
import androidx.compose.ui.platform.ComposeView;

import org.chimeramc.client.R;
import org.chimeramc.client.core.mods.inbuilt.UnifiedMod;
import org.chimeramc.client.core.mods.inbuilt.manager.InbuiltModManager;
import org.chimeramc.client.ui.compose.modmenu.ModMenuDestination;
import org.chimeramc.client.ui.compose.modmenu.ModMenuHost;
import org.chimeramc.client.ui.compose.modmenu.ModMenuState;
import org.chimeramc.client.ui.compose.modmenu.ModMenuStateBuilder;
import org.chimeramc.client.util.AppLog;

import java.util.List;
import java.util.Set;
import java.util.function.UnaryOperator;

/**
 * The Compose presentation of the Mod Menu, layered over the View menu's container.
 *
 * <p>Extracted from {@code ModMenuOverlay} so that class stays inside its size budget. The overlay
 * keeps the View tree, the persistence and the callbacks; this class owns the Compose view, its
 * state, and the mapping from Compose interactions back to the overlay's persistence. That split is
 * also what lets the Compose layer be dropped entirely on a device where it fails to initialise.
 *
 * <p>The Compose tree is added over the already-inflated View tree, so a failure here is caught and
 * logged and the working View menu stays visible rather than a blank window.
 *
 * <p>The package is {@code ...core.mods.inbuilt.overlay} (not the {@code ...launcher.core...} path
 * this file sits under) because that is what the sibling sources declare. A file placed by path with
 * the path-derived package would not be a package-mate of {@code ModMenuOverlay} and could not reach
 * its package-private members.
 */
final class ModMenuScreen {

    /** Called when a module toggle arrives from the Compose UI, so the overlay can persist it. */
    interface ModuleToggle {
        void onToggle(String stableKey, boolean enabled);
    }

    private static final String TAG = "ModMenuScreen";

    private final Activity activity;
    private final View overlayView;
    private final List<UnifiedMod> mods;
    private final Set<String> favoriteKeys;
    private final ModuleToggle moduleToggle;
    private final Runnable onClose;

    private ComposeView composeView;
    private MutableState<ModMenuState> state;
    private boolean attached;

    ModMenuScreen(Activity activity,
                  View overlayView,
                  List<UnifiedMod> mods,
                  Set<String> favoriteKeys,
                  ModuleToggle moduleToggle,
                  Runnable onClose) {
        this.activity = activity;
        this.overlayView = overlayView;
        this.mods = mods;
        this.favoriteKeys = favoriteKeys;
        this.moduleToggle = moduleToggle;
        this.onClose = onClose;
    }

    /** Builds the Compose menu and adds it over the View menu's container. Idempotent. */
    void attach() {
        if (attached || overlayView == null) return;
        attached = true;
        try {
            state = ModMenuHost.state(
                    ModMenuStateBuilder.build(mods, favoriteKeys, ModMenuDestination.MODULES));

            composeView = new ComposeView(activity);
            composeView.setLayoutParams(new FrameLayout.LayoutParams(
                    FrameLayout.LayoutParams.MATCH_PARENT,
                    FrameLayout.LayoutParams.MATCH_PARENT));

            ModMenuHost.setContent(
                    composeView,
                    state,
                    destination -> update(s -> s.withDestination(destination)),
                    query -> update(s -> s.withSearch(query)),
                    (stableKey, enabled) -> {
                        moduleToggle.onToggle(stableKey, enabled);
                        refresh();
                    },
                    stableKey -> {
                        toggleFavorite(stableKey);
                        refresh();
                    },
                    () -> update(s -> s.withFavoritesOnly(!s.getFavoritesOnly())),
                    (key, enabled) -> {
                        InbuiltModManager.getInstance(activity).setModConfigBool(key, enabled);
                        refresh();
                    },
                    onClose::run);

            FrameLayout host = overlayView.findViewById(R.id.mod_menu_container);
            if (host != null) {
                host.addView(composeView);
            } else if (overlayView instanceof ViewGroup) {
                ((ViewGroup) overlayView).addView(composeView);
            }
        } catch (Throwable e) {
            // Compose failing must never take the menu down: the View menu is already inflated
            // underneath, so dropping the Compose layer leaves a working screen.
            AppLog.warnOnce("GlowberryClient", "ModMenuScreen:attach",
                    "The Compose Mod Menu could not start; using the View menu", e);
            composeView = null;
            state = null;
            attached = false;
        }
    }

    /** Rebuilds the rows from the current mod list, preserving the destination and the filters. */
    void refresh() {
        if (state == null) return;
        try {
            final ModMenuState current = state.getValue();
            final ModMenuState rebuilt =
                    ModMenuStateBuilder.build(mods, favoriteKeys, current.getDestination());
            state.setValue(rebuilt
                    .withSearch(current.getSearch())
                    .withFavoritesOnly(current.getFavoritesOnly()));
        } catch (Throwable e) {
            AppLog.warnOnce("GlowberryClient", "ModMenuScreen:refresh",
                    "Could not rebuild the Compose menu rows", e);
        }
    }

    private void update(UnaryOperator<ModMenuState> change) {
        if (state == null) return;
        state.setValue(change.apply(state.getValue()));
    }

    private void toggleFavorite(String stableKey) {
        if (stableKey == null) return;
        final boolean nowFavorite = !favoriteKeys.contains(stableKey);
        if (nowFavorite) {
            favoriteKeys.add(stableKey);
        } else {
            favoriteKeys.remove(stableKey);
        }
        InbuiltModManager.getInstance(activity).setModFavorite(stableKey, nowFavorite);
    }
}

import java.util.List;

/**
 * Splits a module list into favorites and the rest, each sorted by name.
 *
 * <p>Extracted from {@code ModMenuOverlay} as a top-level type: the grouping rule is pure (it reads
 * only a mod's favorite flag and name) and had no reason to be a nested detail of a 3,400-line

 *
 * <p>The package is {@code ...core.mods.inbuilt.overlay} to match the sibling sources in this
 * directory, not the {@code ...launcher.core...} path the file sits under.
 */
final class GroupedMods {

    private final List<UnifiedMod> favorites = new ArrayList<>();
    private final List<UnifiedMod> others = new ArrayList<>();

    void add(UnifiedMod mod, boolean favorite) {
        if (favorite) {
            favorites.add(mod);
        } else {
            others.add(mod);
        }
    }

    void appendTo(List<UnifiedMod> target) {
        sort(favorites);
        sort(others);
        target.addAll(favorites);
        target.addAll(others);
    }

    private void sort(List<UnifiedMod> mods) {
        mods.sort((left, right) -> left.getName().compareToIgnoreCase(right.getName()));
    }
}

## 1. The token-refresh fix (the "constantly sign in" symptom)

A serialised `BedrockAuthManager` is a **snapshot**; `fromJson()` renews nothing. `XalExporter` wrote
that snapshot into the game's XAL directory at launch, so an account signed in a day ago exported an
**expired certificate** — the game started signed out and asked the user to sign in again.

- `MsftAuthManager.refreshStoredAccount()` — deserialises, pulls each step with `getUpToDate()`,
  serialises the renewed chain back, stamps `lastUpdated`.
- Freshness rule `TOKEN_MAX_TRUST_MS = 12h`, **inlined** in `MsftAuthManager` (see §4).
- `MsftAccountStore.updateAuthMaterial()` — replaces one account's material, leaves `active` alone.
- `MinecraftRuntimePreparer` refreshes **before** the launch export. Best-effort: a failure leaves the
  stored chain untouched so an offline launch still exports what it has.

## 2. MSAL: real client id + the full auth chain

- **The client id was the literal `YOUR_CLIENT_ID_HERE`** in two places, so that button could never
  work. `MsftAuthManager.bedrockClientId()` is now the single source of truth;
  `SignInClientIdTest` pins that it is the real 16-hex MSA title id and not a placeholder.
- **`completeMsalLogin()` only returned a username.** It never ran XBL → XSTS → certificate, so MSAL
  "succeeded" while the game launched signed out. It now uses the library's documented seam,
  `BedrockAuthManager.Builder.login(MsaToken)`, and shares `completeLogin()` with the other flows.

Honest limitation: MSAL exposes no refresh token here, so an MSAL-built chain cannot renew itself.
The device-code flow remains the renewing one — which is what the method labels say.

## 3. Un-reds `main` — the `ModMenuOverlay` split

`main` was failing its own `FileSizeBudgetTest`: **3523 lines against a 3400 baseline**, grown by the
already-merged Compose Mod Menu PR. Done in three phases, each compiled and tested:

| Phase | Extracted | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `ModuleFilter` — was a nested enum referenced as `ModMenuOverlay.ModuleFilter` | 31 |
| 2 | `ModMenuScreen` — the Compose presentation + a `ModuleToggle` callback | 155 |
| 3 | `GroupedMods` — the pure favorites/others grouping helper | 41 |

`ModMenuOverlay` is now **3400 lines, at baseline**, and the overlay holds one `ModMenuScreen` field.
The screen never touches storage: it reports a toggle and the overlay persists it through the same
`InbuiltModManager` calls the View menu uses, so the two presentations cannot diverge.

**The trap, for the record.** These files sit under `.../launcher/core/...` but declare
`package org.chimeramc.client.core.mods.inbuilt.overlay` — as do **157 of the 159** siblings in that
directory. A new file placed by path with the path-derived package is *not* a package-mate of them and
cannot reach their package-private members. That is what broke my two earlier attempts. The three new
files follow the sibling convention.

## 4. Why the freshness rule is inlined

Same reason. A new file next to `MsftAuthManager` was not picked up; inlining sidesteps the
package/path mismatch entirely and is what was asked for.

--------------------------
PR #167 was merged at a stale tip: the merge commit's parents were f44af46 and

line would have failed the gate again. The HUD editor is now its own class:

  HudEditorController  431 lines

their "updating programmatically" guards, and the window-parameter switch
between the full-screen menu and the floating tool window. It does not own the
window: it reads the WindowManager and LayoutParams from the menu on every show,
because the menu re-creates them each time and a stale copy would move a window
that no longer exists. Three menu-side effects go back through a Host interface
(navigation highlight, return-to-modules, entrance animation).

  ModMenuOverlay  3523 -> 3123 lines

deliberately NOT lowered, so the room is real and stays available.

even though it sits under .../launcher/core/..., because that is what the 157
sibling sources in that directory declare. A file placed by path with the
path-derived package is not a package-mate of them.

Verified: :app:assembleDebug succeeds; 3764 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors;
FileSizeBudgetTest passes with margin.
EOF

## Three judgement calls worth flagging

1. **The controller doesn't own the window.** It reads `WindowManager`/`LayoutParams` from the menu on every show, because the menu re-creates them each time — a cached copy would move a window that no longer exists. That's a deliberate design choice, not an oversight.

2. **I kept the two "updating programmatically" guards inside the controller.** They exist so setting a slider's progress doesn't loop back through its own listener. Moving the sliders without them would have created an infinite feedback loop — subtle and nasty.

3. **Three menu-side effects go back through a `Host` interface** rather than the controller reaching into the overlay. That's what keeps it extractable and testable.

            try {
                fetchAndCache(appContext, xuid);
            } catch (Throwable error) {

                refreshRunning.set(false);

        // Keyed, so a fetch for the account that just signed in is not dropped by one still running

/**
 * Every surface that shows the player's skin must hear about a skin that arrives late.
 *
 * <p>A sign-in schedules the fetch and the first resolve shows the fallback, so a surface that only
 * resolves on creation shows the default skin until it is recreated. The radial wheel was in that
 * state: it refreshed on attach but never registered a listener, so the real skin did not appear
 * until the wheel was created again — part of the "I signed in and got a default skin" report.
 */

    private static String read(String relative) throws IOException {
        return new String(Files.readAllBytes(Paths.get(relative)), StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
    }

    @Test
    public void theRadialWheelRegistersForSkinUpdates() throws IOException {
        String wheel = read("app/src/main/java/org/chimeramc/client/launcher/core/mods/"
                + "inbuilt/overlay/RadialMenuView.java");
        assertTrue("the wheel must register a skin listener so a late skin reaches it",
                wheel.contains("AccountSkinService.addListener("));
        assertTrue("and it must unregister on detach, so a discarded view is never woken",
                wheel.contains("AccountSkinService.removeListener("));
    }

    @Test
    public void theCapePreviewRegistersForSkinUpdates() throws IOException {
        String preview = read("app/src/main/java/org/chimeramc/client/launcher/core/mods/"
                + "inbuilt/overlay/CapePreviewView.java");
        assertTrue(preview.contains("AccountSkinService.addListener("));
        assertTrue(preview.contains("AccountSkinService.removeListener("));
    }

    @Test
    public void theFetchIsGuardedPerAccountNotGlobally() throws IOException {
        String service = read("app/src/main/java/org/chimeramc/client/core/cosmetics/"
                + "AccountSkinService.java");
        assertTrue("the fetch guard must be keyed by account, or a new sign-in is dropped "
                        + "while the previous account's fetch is still running",
                service.contains("SkinFetchGuard"));
    }
}

import json
body = """## What this changes

Three defects behind **"I sign in and get a random default skin"** and **"skin sync is not constant"**.

**PR 8 of the GlowberryClient series.**

---

## 1. The fetch guard dropped a new sign-in — the main defect

`AccountSkinService` used a single `AtomicBoolean` to stop overlapping fetches. That is correct for
one account and **wrong the moment the account changes**:

1. a fetch for the **previous** account is still in flight
2. the user signs in to a **new** account → `compareAndSet` fails → **the fetch is dropped**
3. the cache is still stamped with the old account's key → `isValidFor` rejects it
4. the preview resolves to **Steve**

The skin did arrive on some later launch, which is exactly why it looked *random* rather than
permanently broken.

**`SkinFetchGuard`** now keys the in-flight fetch by account:
- a request for the **same** account is still refused, so a hot resolve loop cannot start a request storm
- a request for a **different** account **supersedes**, because the account signed in *now* is the one whose skin the user is waiting to see
- a superseded fetch finishing late does **not** clear the newer claim

**Proven by simulation, not assumed:** I compiled the old boolean behaviour behind the same API and ran it:

```
old: account1 allowed=true, account2 allowed=false
OLD FAILS -> defect reproduced, test discriminates
```

## 2. The radial wheel never heard about a late skin

`CapePreviewView` registers an `AccountSkinService` listener while attached. `RadialMenuView`
refreshed on attach but **never registered one**, so the real skin only appeared when the wheel was
recreated. It now registers on attach and unregisters on detach, mirroring the preview's proven
pattern.

## 3. `RadialMenuView` had grown past its own budget

Adding the listener took it to **1952 lines against a 1940 baseline**. Rather than trim comments to
sneak under the gate, the head is now its own class:

| File | Lines |
|---|---|
| `RadialHeadSkin` (new) — skin bitmap, 8×8 head crop, head-only `PreviewScene`, the shared crop rect | 116 |
| `RadialMenuView` | **1952 → 1925** |

The wheel keeps only the drawing decision. Package follows the sibling convention
(`org.chimeramc.client.core.mods.inbuilt.overlay`), as established in PR #168.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `:app:compileDebugJavaWithJavac` | clean |
| `:app:testDebugUnitTest` | **3774 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped** |
| `FileSizeBudgetTest` | **passes** |

New tests: `SkinFetchGuardTest` (7 cases, including the supersede regression and the late-finish

## I found the actual cause of the "random default skin"

Not a cosmetic issue — a **logic bug in the fetch guard**:

1. A fetch for the *previous* account is still in flight
2. You sign in to a *new* account → `compareAndSet` fails → **the fetch is silently dropped**
3. The cache stays stamped with the old account's key → rejected as invalid
4. The preview resolves to **Steve**

The skin arrived on some later launch — which is exactly why it looked *random* instead of broken.

I **proved it by simulation**, not by assertion: compiled the old boolean behind the same API and ran it:

```
old: account1 allowed=true, account2 allowed=false
OLD FAILS -&gt; defect reproduced, test discriminates
```

`SkinFetchGuard` now keys by account: same account still refused (no request storm), **different account supersedes**.

## Second fix: the wheel was deaf

`CapePreviewView` registers a skin listener; `RadialMenuView` **never did** — so a late-arriving skin only showed when the wheel was recreated. Now it registers on attach, unregisters on detach.

## Third: it broke a budget, so I refactored instead of cheating

My listener pushed `RadialMenuView` to **1952 vs a 1940 baseline**. I could have trimmed comments to sneak under — that would have been dishonest. Instead the head became `RadialHeadSkin` (116 lines): **1925**, and the wheel keeps only the drawing decision.

## One thing I did *not* paper over

I tested the GeyserMC endpoint directly: it returns `{}` for XUIDs it has never seen. So for a brand-new player, the account skin resolves to **nothing** and the preview falls back — a **second, independent reason** a new user sees a default skin.

Fixing that means a different skin source (Xbox profile, or on-device capture), which is a bigger change than this PR. It's documented in the PR rather than hidden — **your call on whether that's the next piece**.

## What we actually fixed

The "random default skin" was a **logic bug**, not cosmetics:

&gt; A fetch for the *previous* account was in flight → signing in to a *new* account hit `compareAndSet(false,true)` → **the fetch was silently dropped** → the cache stayed keyed to the old account → rejected as invalid → **Steve**. It arrived on a later launch, which is why it looked random.

Plus the wheel that never registered a listener, so a late skin never reached it.

     * Mints the Minecraft Services bearer for a stored account.
     *
     * <p>The official profile endpoint ({@code api.minecraftservices.com/minecraft/profile}) needs a
     * Minecraft token, not the Bedrock one: Bedrock's XSTS is authorised for
     * {@code multiplayer.minecraft.net}, so it is rejected there. The Minecraft token comes from a
     * separate XSTS exchange against {@code rp://api.minecraftservices.com/}, which the auth library
     * exposes as {@link net.raphimc.minecraftauth.java.JavaAuthManager}.
     *
     * <p>The Bedrock snapshot and the Java snapshot share the same base keys
     * ({@code msaApplicationConfig}, {@code deviceType}, {@code deviceKeyPair}, {@code deviceId},
     * {@code msaToken}, {@code xblDeviceToken}, {@code xblUserToken}), and both carry
     * {@code xboxLiveXstsToken}. So a Bedrock snapshot can be read as a Java one, and the Java chain
     * mints its own token from the shared MSA token rather than needing a second sign-in.
     *
     * <p>Blocking (two network exchanges on a cold token), so the caller must run it off the UI
     * thread. Returns null when no token can be minted, so the caller falls back rather than failing.
     *
     * @return a ready {@code Bearer <token>} header value, or null
     */
    public static String minecraftServicesBearer(MsftAccountStore.MsftAccount account) {
        if (account == null || !hasUsableAuthMaterial(account.serializedAuthManager)) return null;

                    javaAuth.getMinecraftToken().getUpToDate();
            if (token == null) return null;
            String header = token.getAuthorizationHeader();
            return TextUtils.isEmpty(header) ? null : header;
        } catch (Throwable t) {
            // A profile-less account, a network failure or a shape change: report "no token" so the
            // caller uses the legacy lookup rather than losing the skin.
            Log.w(TAG, "Could not mint the Minecraft Services bearer", t);
            return null;
        }
    }

Fetch skins from the official Minecraft Services API (Bedrock-only safe)

The third-party GeyserMC lookup is keyed by XUID and returns nothing for a
player it has never seen, so a brand-new account resolved to no skin and the
preview fell back to Steve. This adds the official source, which every
licensed account has.

  MinecraftSkinFetcher
    - GET https://api.minecraftservices.com/minecraft/profile with the
      account's bearer, and parse the skins array.
    - The ACTIVE entry is preferred (an account can hold several skins); when
      nothing is marked active the first entry with a URL is used, because a
      one-skin profile is common and refusing it would fall back for no reason.
    - Parsing is separate from the request, so the response shape is pinned by
      tests rather than by a player seeing the wrong skin.

  MsftAuthManager.minecraftServicesBearer
    - Mints the bearer from the Java chain's Minecraft token.
    - The Bedrock token cannot be used: its XSTS is authorised for
      multiplayer.minecraft.net, so api.minecraftservices.com rejects it. The
      Java chain exchanges the shared MSA token against
      rp://api.minecraftservices.com/ and returns a Minecraft token, without a
      second sign-in, because the Bedrock snapshot and the Java snapshot share
      the same base keys.

  AccountSkinService
    - Official profile is the PRIMARY source; the legacy GeyserMC lookup is the
      fallback. A player with no Java profile, or a transient bearer failure,
      still gets their skin, so this can only add skins, never remove one.

Bedrock-only safety (the important part)
----------------------------------------
The client's users own Bedrock, not Java Edition, so the skin path must not
require a Java purchase. Verified against the library source:

  - MinecraftLauncherLoginRequest posts to /launcher/login and returns a token;
    it performs NO entitlement check.
  - MinecraftEntitlementsRequest only reads items[].name into a Set. Nothing
    anywhere checks game_minecraft, and it does not throw.
  - minecraftEntitlements is a lazy Holder, fetched only on explicit access.
    This path calls getMinecraftToken() only, so entitlements are never touched.

BedrockOnlySkinLookupTest pins it two ways: a payload test proving a Bedrock-only
entitlement body still yields a skin URL, and a source test proving neither the
service nor the auth manager references the entitlements endpoint or getter, so a
future refactor cannot quietly introduce the requirement.

Verified: :app:assembleDebug succeeds; 3789 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors.
New tests: MinecraftSkinFetcherTest (11) and BedrockOnlySkinLookupTest (4).
EOF

## What this changes

Adds the **official Minecraft Services API** as the primary skin source, so a brand-new account gets
its real skin instead of falling back to Steve.

**PR 9 of the GlowberryClient series.**

---

## The problem this closes

The third-party GeyserMC lookup is keyed by XUID and — verified by calling it — returns `{}` for a
XUID it has never seen:

```
xuid=1                  {} [http=200]
xuid=2535410000000000   {} [http=200]
```

So a new account resolved to *nothing* and the preview fell back. That was the last remaining cause
of the "random default skin" report from #169.

## The fix

| Piece | What it does |
|---|---|
| `MinecraftSkinFetcher` | `GET api.minecraftservices.com/minecraft/profile` with the account's bearer; parses the `skins` array |
| `MsftAuthManager.minecraftServicesBearer` | mints the bearer from the Java chain's Minecraft token |
| `AccountSkinService` | official profile is **primary**; GeyserMC stays as the **fallback** |

**The ACTIVE skin is preferred** (an account can hold several). When nothing is marked active, the
first entry with a URL is used — a one-skin profile is common, and refusing it would fall back for no
reason.

**Why the Bedrock token cannot be used:** its XSTS is authorised for `multiplayer.minecraft.net`, so
`api.minecraftservices.com` rejects it. The Java chain exchanges the shared MSA token against
`rp://api.minecraftservices.com/` and returns a Minecraft token. No second sign-in is needed, because
the Bedrock snapshot and the Java snapshot **share the same base keys** (`msaApplicationConfig`,
`deviceType`, `deviceKeyPair`, `deviceId`, `msaToken`, `xblDeviceToken`, `xblUserToken`).

The fallback is real, not decorative: a player with no Java profile, or a transient bearer failure,
still gets their skin from the legacy lookup. **This change can only add skins, never remove one.**

---

## Bedrock-only safety — verified, not assumed

You were right to stop me here. The client's users own **Bedrock, not Java Edition**, so a
`game_minecraft` entitlement requirement would break the skin for *every* user. I checked the library
source directly:

| Question | Finding |
|---|---|
| Does `MinecraftLauncherLoginRequest` check entitlements? | **No.** It POSTs `/launcher/login` and returns a token. No entitlement call at all. |
| Does `MinecraftEntitlementsRequest` enforce `game_minecraft`? | **No.** It only reads `items[].name` into a `Set`. Nothing checks it; nothing throws. |
| Are entitlements fetched on this path? | **No.** `minecraftEntitlements` is a lazy `Holder`, fetched only on explicit access. This path calls `getMinecraftToken()` only. |

**No `MinecraftAuthManager` shim was needed** — the library already mints the token without touching
entitlements. I did not add a skip-entitlements variant because there is no entitlement step to skip;
adding one would have been dead code that *looked* like it was doing something.

`BedrockOnlySkinLookupTest` pins this two ways:
1. a **payload test** — a Bedrock-only entitlement body (`product_minecraft_bedrock` present,
   `game_minecraft` absent) still yields a skin URL from the profile;
2. a **source test** — neither the service nor the auth manager references the entitlements endpoint
   or getter, so a future refactor cannot quietly introduce the requirement.

I verified the test discriminates: injecting `getMinecraftEntitlements()` into the path makes it fail.
